repost.content:
We get dozens of applications to partner with Buffer every single day. They all used to land in the same queue for manual review. This process was time-consuming, and most of the calls were obvious either way.

So Pierre from our team built an agent that handles the clear-cut ones: the applications that plainly fit, and the ones that plainly don't. Here's how it works:

• It's built on top of Dub.co, our partner platform, where all the application data lives. 
• Based on our criteria, it decides which partner group each accepted applicant belongs to, since each group has its own expectations and agreement. 
• From there, it handles the communication automatically, whether that's a rejection or onboarding the new partner, and posts to the program's public Slack channel so the team can review and triage.

For this process, LLMs were the clear choice. Obvious cases don't need judgment; they need speed. Clearing them automatically buys back the time we used to spend sorting a queue, which now goes into engaging with our partners.

And the applications that aren't black and white? Those still get a human every time. Pierre gets one ping a day with the borderline cases and reviews them properly. He logs his reasoning on each, so the agent's mental model improves with every run and captures more of the edge cases over time.

The goal was never to take people out of the process. It was to put our judgment where it's genuinely needed.

I'll keep sharing the AI-assisted processes we've come to rely on and real use cases from the team each week.

Back then, it was just the two of us, with a very small but dedicated team, iterating for years. Failing multiple times.

Showing products that users didn't even want to test!

But we never gave up.

Our decisions were often wrong. Certainly more often than not! We kept trying.

Now we’ve shipped something people love.

Worth every sleepless night. Every sacrifice.

The best employees don’t need to be told what to do.

Neither does Viktor.

Grateful to Zhenya Loginov, Cecilia Wang and Bilal Mobarik for leading this round. Grateful to our team, our earliest users, and everyone who believed this category could be bigger than chat.

posts.content:
We've been obsessing a lot about creating the best possible AI support experience Dub.co.

And I think we've found the magic formula.

The stack:
✦ Mintlify → docs + help articles
✦ Upstash vector → vector search
✦ AI SDK + Claude Sonnet → LLM/retrieval
✦ Plain → support infra

Here's how it works:

We consolidated our docs + help articles on Mintlify (best-in-class docs platform) so all our support content is now in one place.

On every push to main, we sync changes to our Upstash Vector DB.
We also built a custom chat interface that retrieves content from Upstash Vector and generates responses via AI SDK + Claude sonnet.

The best part: The AI agent uses 𝚝𝚘𝚘𝚕() from AI SDK to retrieve the user's workspace / partner data to provide accurate responses.

Finally, if the user needs to speak to a human, we generate a 𝚃𝚒𝚌𝚔𝚎𝚝𝚄𝚙𝚕𝚘𝚊𝚍 UI that lets users upload screenshots + add more context, before creating a ticket on Plain.

Cherry on top: The chat interface is embeddable, so we're able to embed it both in our Mintlify docs + support portal 👇

Since we launched this, it's been a gamechanger for scaling support – reducing support workload and creating a much better experience for our users.

Highly recommend giving this a try!
